description: Signed-AND-fresh: four required properties — pinned source, signature, grant-carried sequence floor, tamper-evident mark. Each is independently necessary.
note: Scenarios 1-5 are the core claim. Scenarios 6-9 are ablations: each removes one property and the specific attack must succeed (expected=ALLOW or REFUSED_TAMPERED depending on the property). If an ablation does not return the expected failure, that property was not load-bearing.

scenarios.label: E
scenarios.description: Clean — TTL-valid, conditions unchanged, sequence current, mark current
scenarios.why: All four properties satisfied. Clean grant, fresh response, mark current.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.description: TTL-valid drift — conditions changed, sequence current, timestamp gate misses this
scenarios.why: Sequence is current (15 >= 10) and signature valid, but source conditions changed. Role downgraded from dev-reader to restricted. Timestamp-only gate returns ALLOW — this is the divergence cell inherited from CLAIM-24.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.description: Replay attack — genuine pre-revocation signed response, sequence below grant floor

source_response.note: This is a genuine pre-revocation response — signature is valid, but sequence 8 predates grant issuance at sequence 10. Role was dev-reader before the revocation event.

scenarios.why: Signature is valid — this is a genuine issuer response. But sequence 8 < grant.sequence_at_issue 10. The grant-carried floor rejects it. Signature-only gate returns ALLOW. This is the window signature-only gates cannot close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.description: Cold-start replay — no stored mark, floor must come from grant

source_response.note: Pre-revocation response. Signature valid. Sequence 8 predates revocation.

scenarios.why: Gate has no stored mark — cold start or post-restart. Floor is derived from grant.sequence_at_issue=10. Response sequence 8 < 10. Gate refuses. Without grant-carried floor, cold start has no baseline and replay succeeds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.description: Mark rewind — attacker rewound the high-water mark, tamper must be detected

source_response.note: Pre-revocation response. The mark was rewound from 15 to 5 so this sequence appears above the mark.

gate_state.mark_tamper_note: Mark was 15 at last valid read. Rewound to 5 by attacker. Gate must detect monotonicity violation.

scenarios.why: Sequence 8 > rewound mark 5, so a non-monotonic gate would return ALLOW. Tamper-evident gate detects mark was lowered (not append-only) and refuses. If mark storage is rewindable, rollback moves from source layer to mark layer — same attack one level down.

scenarios.label: A1
scenarios.description: ABLATION: Drop grant-carried floor — cold-start replay must succeed (ALLOW expected)
scenarios.ablation_note: Grant has no sequence_at_issue. Gate has no stored mark (cold start). Gate has no floor from any source. If the gate still refuses, the grant-carried floor was not load-bearing — something else blocked it.

source_response.note: Pre-revocation response. Without a floor, this cannot be rejected on sequence grounds.

scenarios.failure_mode: cold-start replay passed — no floor from any source
scenarios.why: ABLATION EXPECTED FAILURE. Without grant-carried floor and without stored mark, cold-start replay has nothing to be rejected against. Gate must return ALLOW here to prove the grant-carried floor (scenario 4) was load-bearing.

scenarios.label: A2
scenarios.description: ABLATION: Rewindable mark — rollback must reopen the attack (ALLOW expected)
scenarios.ablation_note: Grant floor is 5 (legitimately reachable — real grant was issued at seq 5). Replayed sequence 8 >= floor 5, so floor passes. The only remaining guard is tamper detection. With it disabled, 8 > rewound mark 5 and gate accepts. Floor is NOT removed in this ablation — only tamper detection is stripped. This is the clean isolation.

source_response.note: Pre-revocation response. Sequence 8 >= grant floor 5 — floor passes. Mark was rewound from 12 to 5 (a legitimately reachable value — real grant existed at seq 5). Tamper detection disabled in this ablation.

gate_state.mark_tamper_note: Mark WAS at 12, rewound to 5 by attacker. 5 is legitimately reachable (real grant at seq 5) so it does not look obviously impossible. Only monotonicity check would catch this. Tamper detection disabled in this ablation.

scenarios.failure_mode: rewound mark accepted — mark lowered without detection
scenarios.why: ABLATION EXPECTED FAILURE. Floor passes (8 >= 5). Without tamper detection, the monotonicity violation goes undetected and 8 > rewound mark 5. Gate returns ALLOW. Tamper detection is isolated as the sole load-bearing property in this cell.

scenarios.label: A3
scenarios.description: ABLATION: Unpinned source — substitution must succeed (ALLOW expected)
scenarios.ablation_removes: enforcement of grant.source_address at execution time
scenarios.ablation_note: Gate reads from runtime-supplied address instead of grant.source_address. Attacker substitutes a friendly source returning ALLOW state.

source_response.note: Response from SUBSTITUTED friendly source. Real source would return restricted/refused.

gate_state.substitution_note: source_address_runtime differs from grant.source_address. Gate reads from runtime address in this ablation.

scenarios.failure_mode: substituted source accepted — runtime address used instead of grant address
scenarios.why: ABLATION EXPECTED FAILURE. Without source pinning, the gate reads from the attacker-supplied address. Friendly source returns ALLOW. This proves that pinning source_address inside the grant (scenario 2 defense) is load-bearing.

scenarios.label: A4
scenarios.description: ABLATION: No signature — forged response must pass (ALLOW expected)
scenarios.ablation_note: Gate does not verify response signature. Attacker presents forged response with high sequence and ALLOW conditions.

source_response.note: FORGED response. Signature is invalid. Gate must verify signature. If gate skips verification, sequence 50 >= floor 10 and ALLOW is returned.

scenarios.failure_mode: forged response accepted — invalid signature not checked
scenarios.why: ABLATION EXPECTED FAILURE. Gate skips signature check. Forged response has high sequence (50 >= 10) and ALLOW conditions. Gate returns ALLOW. This proves signature verification is load-bearing.

scenarios.label: A2-overlap
scenarios.description: OVERLAP ASSERTION: Both grant floor and tamper detection cover this cell — defense-in-depth zone
scenarios.ablation_note: This is not an isolated control. It documents the defense-in-depth zone from the original confounded A2: grant floor 10 > replayed sequence 8, AND mark is tampered. Both properties independently catch this attack. Registered so any future change that quietly drops either guard shows up as a regression.

source_response.note: Pre-revocation response. Sequence 8 < grant floor 10 — floor would catch it. Mark also rewound to 5 with tamper flag set — tamper detection would also catch it. Both guards active.

gate_state.mark_tamper_note: Mark rewound from 12 to 5. Tamper detected. Floor (10) also exceeds replayed sequence (8). This cell has two independent guards.

scenarios.why: OVERLAP ASSERTION. Gate fires REFUSED_TAMPERED (tamper check comes before floor check in evaluation order). If tamper detection were dropped, floor would still catch it (8 < 10). If floor were dropped, tamper detection would still catch it. Defense-in-depth — both guards must remain for this cell to be fully protected.
